Tomorrow you do not have to come to work at all.
You had better rest quietly at home.

examples.trans: I will definitely help the two of you get closer.

examples.text: Спасибо за приглашение, я обязательно приду.
examples.trans: Thank you for the invitation, I will definitely come.

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go through, to pass; to come along', paired with 'проходить'.

related.gloss: not to to go through (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Ты обязательно пройдёшь полное обследование.
examples.trans: You will definitely undergo a full medical checkup.

examples.text: Пройдите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Go through, please.

examples.text: Потом пройдёт.
examples.trans: Then it passes.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

examples.text: Ты обязательно пройдёшь полное обследование.
examples.trans: You will definitely undergo a full medical checkup.

examples.text: Делаете сегодня дополнительную выручку нашему бару?
examples.trans: Are you making extra revenue for our bar today?

examples.text: Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'следование'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'medical checkup / examination' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты обязательно пройдёшь полное обследование.
examples.trans: You will definitely undergo a full medical checkup.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, я Виктор от Елены на обследование.
examples.trans: Hello, I am Victor, sent by Elena for a checkup.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'руга'). Common feminine noun meaning 'female friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня подруга работает в поликлинике.
examples.trans: My friend works as chief doctor at the clinic.

examples.text: Я подругу приглашу в гости.
examples.trans: I'll invite a female friend over.

examples.text: Она моя лучшая подруга.
examples.trans: She is my best friend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Тем более я гениальный шеф-повар.
examples.trans: Especially since I am a brilliant head chef.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ликлиника'). Common feminine noun meaning 'clinic' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня подруга работает в поликлинике.
examples.trans: My friend works as chief doctor at the clinic.

examples.text: Завтра в два часа в поликлинике?
examples.trans: Tomorrow at two o'clock at the clinic?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лена, у меня всё в порядке!
examples.trans: Lena, everything is fine with me!

examples.text: Я потом тебе всё подробно расскажу.
examples.trans: I will tell you everything in detail later.

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Лена, у меня всё в порядке!
examples.trans: Lena, everything is fine with me!

examples.text: Скажи, у тебя точно всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Tell me, is everything really alright with you?

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку.
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.
